affiliations: , New York University - Leonard N. Stern School of Business - Department of Economics,  and National Bank of Belgium

detail.title: Micro and Macro Cost-Price Dynamics in Normal Times and During Inflation Surges

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of New York Staff Report No. 1195
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We develop a unified approach to studying cost-price dynamics in the cross-section of firms in order to jointly explain the time series of aggregate inflation and the frequency of price changes, both during normal times and inflation surges. A key novelty is the use of microdata on firms' prices and production costs to construct an empirical measure of price gaps-the deviation between a firm's listed and optimal price. Conditional on the path of aggregate cost shocks extracted from the data, a state-dependent pricing model with strategic complementarities accounts well for both the linear cost-price dynamics of the prepandemic period and the nonlinear increase in inflation and frequency of price adjustment that followed.

title: Group Network Multivariate GARCH
affiliations: Business School, University of Sussex, University of Pennsylvania and University of Miami

detail.title: Group Network Multivariate GARCH

keywords: portfolio optimization JEL Classification codes: C53

detail.abstract: Traditional multivariate generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH) models often become infeasible in high-dimensional settings because of the curse of dimensionality. We propose a group-network multivariate GARCH model in which the propagation of past return shocks and past conditional variances across assets is governed by a latent group structure and an observed network adjacency matrix. By imposing network- and group-based restrictions, the proposed model substantially reduces the parameter dimension, thereby facilitating estimation in large cross-sections. We establish the large-sample properties of an estimator that jointly estimates the model parameters and latent group memberships via an iterative optimization algorithm. Monte Carlo simulations support the theoretical results. An empirical application to S&P 100 constituents over 2015-2022 shows that the proposed model delivers economically meaningful gains in out-of-sample portfolio performance compared to standard multivariate GARCH specifications.

title: When Technology Manages: Workers, Unions, and Collective Bargaining in the Age of AI
affiliations: and

detail.title: When Technology Manages: Workers, Unions, and Collective Bargaining in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence and digital technologies are transforming work, but their consequences for workers and unions remain unclear. We distinguish displacement, augmentation, and monitoring technologies and argue that each reshapes job stability, workplace interaction, and union leverage differently. Using survey evidence from workers in Western countries, we show that augmentation and monitoring are associated with higher unionization, whereas displacement predicts the reverse, reflecting how different technologies reshape working conditions. We then analyze a novel dataset we assembled of more than 40,000 Canadian collective bargaining agreements from 1993 to 2025, showing that exposure shapes not only membership but also what unions bargain for. Augmentation and monitoring are linked to stronger protections on training, governance, notice, and surveillance, while displacement is associated with weaker protections. Together, these findings suggest that the future of work is not predetermined by technology alone but is also negotiated at the bargaining table.

title: Macroprudential Policy for a Low-Carbon Economy: The Case of Cross Border Funding in China
affiliations: Council on Economic Policies and University of Zurich - Department Finance

detail.title: Macroprudential Policy for a Low-Carbon Economy: The Case of Cross Border Funding in China
detail.abstract: China is opening further space for cross-border funding for the low-carbon transition - to diversify financing sources, support potentially underfunded entities, and attract inbound foreign investment alongside its already deep domestic funding base. Since last year, policymakers have been easing macroprudential rules that limit how much Chinese firms can borrow from abroad. By early 2026, at least USD 300 million had been raised under the pilot - a modest figure for now, but one that is likely to grow as experience accumulates and processes get streamlined. The global interest rate environment will play a leading role in determining how far this goes. This policy brief unpacks what is happening and why it matters.

title: High-Speed Rail and Scientific Collaboration: Evidence from China
affiliations: and

detail.title: High-Speed Rail and Scientific Collaboration: Evidence from China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the effect of China's high-speed rail (HSR) on inter-city scientific collaboration and examines whether this effect varies systematically with the complexity of scientific fields. Combining the universe of HSR openings between 2008 and 2020 with OpenAlex publication records, we construct a panel spanning 33,793 Chinese city pairs. Using a staggered difference-indifferences estimator, we find that HSR increases co-publications among city-pairs with existing collaborative ties by 35.2 percent at the city-pair level. Disaggregating across twenty scientific fields, we show that this effect is quite heterogeneous. Field-level treatment effects range from 19.8 to 45.1 percent, and their magnitude is positively and significantly correlated with average team sizea proxy of the fields' complexity. These results are consistent with the view that faceto-face interaction is still important for knowledge production requiring deep divisions of cognitive labour, and they carry direct implications for the design of transportation and innovation policy.

title: Banks' Strategic Trading of Investment Securities and Systemic Risk
affiliations: University of St. Gallen - School of Finance,  and IESEG School of Management

detail.title: Banks' Strategic Trading of Investment Securities and Systemic Risk
detail.abstract: This study examines how banks’ strategic trading of investment securities, motivated by earnings management or regulatory arbitrage incentives, affects bank risk. We find that strategic trading is positively associated with individual bank risk. We further show that such trading is linked to higher contributions to systemic risk and greater exposure to system-wide distress. To identify the underlying mechanism, we show that strategic trading increases systemic risk primarily by amplifying banks’ exposures to macroeconomic and finance risk factors. These results highlight a novel channel through which discretionary portfolio choices translate into greater aggregate financial fragility. Overall, our findings provide evidence consistent with unintended adverse consequences of banks’ strategic securities trading for the stability of the financial system.

title: No Surveys Required: Small Language Models Enable Scalable ESG Extraction from Annual Reports
affiliations: University of Lausanne - Faculty of Business and Economics (HEC Lausanne), University of Lausanne and University of Lausanne - Faculty of Business and Economics (HEC Lausanne)

detail.title: No Surveys Required: Small Language Models Enable Scalable ESG Extraction from Annual Reports

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding

detail.abstract: Climate disclosure mandates are expanding, while ESG teams remain too small to cover all holdings, monitor compliance, and conduct deep analysis simultaneously. Survey-based frameworks reach only willing participants, leaving non-participating companies, recent acquisitions, and competitors unassessed. We show that AI can extract ESG information directly from published annual reports, achieving 80% accuracy on a 36-criterion framework without input from the reporting entity. Tested on 30 Swiss real estate annual reports in three languages, compact AI models running on standard office computers perform within one percentage point of costly cloud services while keeping portfolio data on-premise. The key finding is not that one system dominates, but that different configurations fit different workflows: precision-oriented models reduce false alarms in portfolio screening, whereas recalloriented models better support compliance tasks where missed disclosures carry legal risk. Off-the-shelf models already deliver production-grade accuracy without customization or training investment. Since report quality explains more performance variation than model choice, we propose a tiered review process: automatic acceptance for straightforward reports, targeted verification for flagged cases, and full manual review for high-stakes or ambiguous documents. More broadly, AI-enabled extraction can turn unstructured disclosures into structured inputs for automated workflows, reducing repetitive analyst workload and bringing qualitative analysis closer to the rigor and scalability of quantitative methods.

title: The Impact of Geopolitical Risk on U.S. Natural Gas E&P Investments: A Time-Varying Quantile Causality Approach
affiliations: University of Central Oklahoma, University of Central Oklahoma and University of Central Oklahoma

detail.title: The Impact of Geopolitical Risk on U.S. Natural Gas E&P Investments: A Time-Varying Quantile Causality Approach
detail.abstract: This paper employs a time-varying quantile causality framework to examine the impact of geopolitical risk on the volatility of energy sector investment, proxied by U.S. gas rig counts. By allowing the causal relationship to vary across time and the conditional distribution, the analysis captures nonlinear and state-dependent dynamics that conventional approaches may overlook. The results indicate that the effect of geopolitical risk is asymmetric and episodic. During periods of moderate volatility, geopolitical risk does not exert a statistically significant influence, suggesting that investors largely discount such disturbances. In contrast, under conditions of elevated market stress, geopolitical risk becomes a significant driver of investment volatility, with responses consistent with a real options mechanism. Our study finds a massive causality spells from 2016 onward, perfectly aligning with the exact moment the U.S. began exporting LNG to the global market, suddenly making domestic rig operators highly vulnerable to international geopolitical shocks. Overall, the empirical specification controls for key supply-side fundamentals (gas storage), price dynamics, and broader macroeconomic conditions, including interest rates and equity market performance, allowing the analysis to isolate the independent role of geopolitical risk. Overall, the findings highlight the state-dependent nature of investment responses to geopolitical uncertainty and contribute to the literature on upstream energy investment dynamics.

title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Energy and Resource Sharing in Indian Residential Communities
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Bombay

detail.title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Energy and Resource Sharing in Indian Residential Communities
detail.abstract: The increasing adoption of residential solar photovoltaics and battery storage has led to growing interest in community energy sharing as a way to improve local energy utilization and reduce dependence on the grid. However, the economic performance of such systems depends on how energy resources are owned and shared within the community. In particular, the comparative benefits of private, centralized, and hybrid configurations are not yet clearly understood under a consistent framework. This study investigates the techno-economic performance of residential energy communities by comparing different system configurations that integrate peer-to-peer (P2P) energy sharing and battery storage. A generic simulation framework is developed to enable a fair comparison across ownership structures and battery technologies. The findings indicate that energy sharing improves local energy utilization and reduces grid imports across all configurations. However, the resulting economic benefits differ across system designs. Private systems with P2P sharing tend to provide better economic returns for individual prosumers. In contrast, centralized systems offer lower overall system costs and balanced stakeholder benefits, combining favorable investor payback with reduced energy costs for users without upfront investment. Hybrid systems show better grid interaction but are less economically viable for the central operator. Battery technology also plays a role in system performance, particularly in improving energy autonomy. Overall, the results suggest that the performance of community energy systems depends not only on technical improvements but also on how costs and benefits are distributed among participants.

title: Intertemporal Arbitrage and Optimal Operation ofPumped Hydro Energy Storage
affiliations: Comillas Pontifical University - Department of Financial Management and Simon Fraser University (SFU), University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Finance Area

detail.title: Intertemporal Arbitrage and Optimal Operation ofPumped Hydro Energy Storage
detail.abstract: Hydropower is a renewable and flexible energy source that provides essentialstorage capacity and enhances grid stability. Among storage technologies,pumped hydro energy storage (PHES) remains the most cost-effective solu-tion for long-duration energy storage and plays a key role in power systemswith increasing penetration of variable renewable energy. As electricity pricesbecome more relevant under the energy transition, understanding the opti-mal operation and valuation of PHES assets is increasingly important froma financial perspective. This paper develops a market-based framework thatmodels a PHES facility as a profit-maximizing asset operating in liberalizedelectricity markets. Using an optimal control approach calibrated with real-life technical and operational parameters of the La Muela pumped storageplant and observed electricity prices from the Spanish wholesale market, themodel derives an economically intuitive trigger (switching) price that gov-erns optimal pumping and generation decisions while accounting for reservoirwater inventory dynamics and electricity price uncertainty. The results showthat inventory dynamics and electricity price seasonality are central to PHESvaluation and optimal operation

title: Regime Shifts in the Relationship Between Crude Oil Returns and U.S. Partisan Conflict
affiliations: Aalborg University - Department of Mathematical Sciences and University of Exeter

detail.title: Regime Shifts in the Relationship Between Crude Oil Returns and U.S. Partisan Conflict
detail.abstract: Political polarization has become an important source of macroeconomic uncertainty, yet its relationship with commodity markets remains poorly understood. This paper investigates the evolving link between U.S. partisan conflict and crude oil returns using a Markov-switching Granger causality approach that incorporates time-varying volatility and correlation, allowing for the endogenous detection of structural breaks in predictive relationships. Using monthly data from 1981 to 2025, we identify two distinct regimes. Prior to 2009, oil shocks systematically Granger-caused increases in partisan conflict, highlighting the destabilizing effects of import dependence and global supply disruptions. After the global financial crisis and the shale boom, this predictive channel largely disappeared, with oil prices no longer providing consistent information about domestic political polarization. Our findings challenge the conventional view that oil prices reliably signal U.S. political conflict, suggesting instead that their informational value depends on broader energy and political conditions.

title: The Epistemic Splinternet: How Geopolitically Fragmented AI Ecosystems Are Producing Incompatible Realities and Why This Threatens Diplomacy, Commerce, and the Academic

detail.title: The Epistemic Splinternet: How Geopolitically Fragmented AI Ecosystems Are Producing Incompatible Realities and Why This Threatens Diplomacy, Commerce, and the Academic
detail.abstract: Existing analyses of internet fragmentation have focused on infrastructure, governance and market competition. This paper argues that the more fundamental and least examined consequence is epistemological. That is the emergence of AI systems that have been trained within these different geopolitical ecosystems, so they have learned structurally incompatible versions of reality. Drawing on empirical research into AI model censorship, the recursive contamination of internet training data, and the mechanisms of state-directed propaganda laundering, the paper identifies five mechanisms through which epistemic divergence is being encoded into AI systems at a civilisational scale. It argues that this divergence poses qualitatively distinct threats to diplomatic coordination, commercial trust, and the integrity of the academic knowledge record, threats that affect developed and developing nations alike. Though developing nations face the additional risk of epistemic colonialisation by AI systems that have no incentive to represent their societies accurately. The paper introduces the concept of Epistemic Balkanisation to describe the structural condition in which AI systems trained in different geopolitical spheres cannot agree on basic matters of historical fact, societal description, or causal attribution and where each system's version of reality is self-reinforcing through recursive training loops that progressively narrow the distance between state-directed narrative and baseline epistemic architecture. It concludes by proposing a governance framework grounded in epistemic transparency standards, cross-sphere AI auditing and the case of India's strategic position as a potential interoperability bridge in a fragmenting global knowledge ecosystem.

title: The Brandcore Strength Model

detail.title: The Brandcore Strength Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author publishes professionally as Simeon Taiwo. He is the founder of Clarylife Global and Senior Partner at BrandingSchool.NG. The BrandCore Strength Model was developed through applied consulting practice at Clarylife Global and is being developed into a commercial diagnostic tool. No external funding or third-party interests influenced the research or its conclusions.

detail.abstract:
Brand strength measurement has been approached from multiple theoretical and commercial perspectives over the past four decades. From Aaker's five-dimension model to Young and Rubicam's Brand Asset Valuator, from Keller's Customer-Based Brand Equity pyramid to the more recent simplifications of brand strength into two-variable multiplicative formulas, the field has produced a rich but fragmented landscape of tools.

This paper reviews the existing body of knowledge on brand strength measurement, identifies persistent gaps in current frameworks, and proposes The BrandCore Strength Model (BCSM) as an integrated evolution that addresses those gaps. The BCSM extends the established multiplicative logic of Visibility multiplied by Reputation into a four-variable model: Visibility, Net Reputation, Differentiation, and Loyalty. It introduces a net reputation formulation that accounts for the asymmetric impact of negative perception, a diagnostic pathology layer that maps score patterns to specific brand conditions, and an integration architecture that connects the quantitative model to established proprietary brand theory, including the Awareness-Experience-Memory brand journey, the Three Cardinals of Every Solid Brand, and the Suspect-to-Trusted trust sequence.

The model is designed for practical application in emerging markets, with particular attention to the African and Nigerian business context, where formal market research infrastructure is often limited but the need for brand measurement is acute.

title: A Novel in-Situ Wireless Monitoring of Bearing Cage Vibration and Skidding via Integrated Triboelectric and MEMS Sensing
affiliations: Chongqing University, Tsinghua University, Chongqing University, Beijing University of Chemical Technology, Tsinghua University, Chongqing University and Tongji University - Department  of Cardio-Pulmonary  Circulation

detail.title: A Novel in-Situ Wireless Monitoring of Bearing Cage Vibration and Skidding via Integrated Triboelectric and MEMS Sensing
detail.abstract: To overcome the limitations of traditional bearing condition monitoring methods, such as long vibration transmission paths and weak fault features being easily corrupted by noise, this study proposes a novel wireless self-sensing intelligent bearing for in-situ bearing skidding and vibration detection (SV-WSB). Different from conventional external monitoring methods, the proposed structure integrates microelectromechanical system (MEMS) vibration sensor, triboelectric sensing unit, signal processing circuit, and a Wi-Fi transmission module directly onto the bearing cage, enabling synchronous acquisition and wireless transmission of multi-source signals during bearing operation. The triboelectric module was designed in a floating freestanding mode to capture cage rotational characteristics without interfering with bearing motion, while the MEMS sensor was used for direct perception of cage vibration and transient responses. Experiments were conducted under steady-state, acceleration–deceleration, variable-load, and external impact conditions. The triboelectric signal was used to monitor cage rotational speed and skidding ratio, and the measured cage speed showed only 0.2% deviation compared with high-speed camera measurements. The vibration signal demonstrated high sensitivity to transient impact excitation and unstable operating conditions. In addition, the influences of dielectric material and electrode gap on triboelectric output performance were systematically investigated. A CNN-Transformer-based multi-source information fusion model was further established for bearing fault diagnosis, achieving higher diagnostic accuracy than methods using only a single sensing signal. The proposed SV-WSB provides a compact and effective solution for intelligent bearing condition monitoring and fault diagnosis.

title: IndoCEPH: Cephalometric Radiograph Dataset for Anatomical Landmark Detection of the Indonesian Population
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: IndoCEPH: Cephalometric Radiograph Dataset for Anatomical Landmark Detection of the Indonesian Population
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Cephalometric radiography, which displays craniofacial structures, is a key tool in dentistry, serving as the gold standard for analyzing, evaluating, and diagnosing dental and skeletal relationships. Cephalometric analysis identifies landmarks and measures angles on radiographs. However, this process is time-consuming, inconsistent, and requires experience. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been extensively explored for cephalometric landmark identification to improve accuracy and efficiency. Despite efforts to develop automated landmark detection systems, they remain inadequate for orthodontic applications due to the lack of reliable datasets.Methods: To address this gap, we propose IndoCEPH, designed to support the development of robust AI solutions for quantitative morphometric analysis. Differences in facial morphology across various racial or ethnic groups are widely acknowledged, highlighting the importance of region-specific datasets. IndoCEPH was developed as a publicly available dataset consist of lateral cephalometric radiographs from the Indonesian population annotated with 17 anatomical landmarks by oral and maxillofacial radiology experts. Radiographs were selected using quality-based inclusion and exclusion criteria and included various malocclusion conditions. Dataset performance was evaluated using a deep learning-based landmark detection model and compared with a public dataset using localization metrics and detection performance metrics.Results: Experimental results using the IndoCEPH dataset demonstrated that the model achieved a mean radial error (MRE) of 1.00 mm and a successful detection rate (SDR) of 86.9% within a 2 mm range. The model also achieved a precision of 0.881, recall of 0.743, and mAP@50 of 0.731. Compared with the public dataset, IndoCEPH demonstrated improved overall landmark detection performance and successfully detected all 17 anatomical landmarks.Conclusions: The dataset provides valuable insights and fosters progress in landmark identification. Additionally, it can be applied in dental and skeletal age determination along with anthropometric comparisons across populations.

title: Metabolic Plasticity and Climate Resilience: A Bio-Economic Framework for Sustainable Biofortification and Nutritional Security in Bimodal Savannas
affiliations: Osun State University

detail.title: Metabolic Plasticity and Climate Resilience: A Bio-Economic Framework for Sustainable Biofortification and Nutritional Security in Bimodal Savannas
detail.abstract: Sustainable food systems in tropical bimodal savannas are increasingly threatened by climate-induced volatility, which compromises both the quantity and nutritional density of staple crops. While traditional agricultural research prioritizes harvest volume, this study investigates "metabolic plasticity"—the physiological capacity of food matrices to maintain stable nutritional profiles under environmental flux. We evaluated the "production-to-consumption" journey of seven biofortified maize resources, integrating field-level climate resilience with high-resolution laboratory profiling of the grain ionome, essential amino acids, and carotenoid content. Our findings identify reproductive synchronization (ASI) as a critical upstream gatekeeper for food system reliability. The elite variant MG 4 demonstrated superior metabolic plasticity, maintaining a 1.2-day synchronisation threshold that secured a high-density nutritional floor (3117 µg/100g Provitamin A; 1.89 g/100g Lysine) during high-stress seasons. In contrast, local varieties reached a physiological tipping point beyond a 5-day stress threshold, leading to a collapse in nutrient partitioning. To translate these biochemical findings into food system policy, an Asset vs. Investment (AvI) bio-economic framework was applied. The synchronized MG 4 variant achieved a 100% Asset Reliability Score, proving that climate-resilient biofortified germplasm can systematically displace the recurring public health costs of pharmaceutical interventions. This study provides a multidisciplinary blueprint for transforming food systems by prioritizing "Nutrient Delivery Reliability" to secure the health of vulnerable populations in high-uncertainty agroecologies.

title: JCCDB v1.2 — Cryptographic Audit Hash and Macroeconomic Price Correction for Reproducible LLM-Based Construction Cost Diagnostics

detail.title: JCCDB v1.2 — Cryptographic Audit Hash and Macroeconomic Price Correction for Reproducible LLM-Based Construction Cost Diagnostics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and Representative Director of The Horizons Co., Ltd., which operates HORIZON SHIELD, the production system described in this paper. This relationship is disclosed in full in the paper's Acknowledgments section.

detail.abstract:
We present JCCDB v1.2, a substantive extension to the Japan Construction Cost Database (JCCDB), an open structured dataset supporting LLM-based construction cost diagnostic systems for consumer protection.

First, we introduce a cryptographic audit hash mechanism based on SHA-256 that provides reproducibility guarantees for diagnostic outputs: identical inputs always produce the same 12-character (48-bit) audit hashes printed on consumer-facing PDF reports, enabling vendor-neutral, client-side verification during contractor negotiations.

Second, we describe a War Price Coefficient (WPC) subsystem that automatically incorporates manufacturer price-change announcements into monthly price corrections, addressing the documented exploitation of material price volatility in renovation contractor fraud. The current deployed coefficient is ×1.0935 (+9.35%, Hormuz Strait/Iran-conflict baseline), computed from a weighted composite of seven CGPI series and four manufacturer announcements.

We demonstrate the production deployment of both mechanisms within HORIZON SHIELD, a Cloudflare Workers-based diagnostic service, and validate hash output stability. Theoretical collision analysis using the birthday-bound approximation indicates collision probability below 2×10⁻⁵ for realistic deployment scales within the 48-bit truncated hash space.

The mechanisms described are designed to align with the recording and human-oversight principles of EU AI Act Article 12 and Article 14 (Regulation 2024/1689, applicable to high-risk systems from August 2, 2026), and are released under CC-BY 4.0 to support independent replication.

title: Uncertainty about "Uncertainty"
affiliations: Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo Institute of Technology - School of Engineering, Paula and Gregory Chow Institute for Studies in Economics, Xiamen University and Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Uncertainty about "Uncertainty"
detail.abstract: The past twenty years have witnessed growing claims of ignorance in firm disclosures, as managers increasingly attribute outcomes to "uncertainty" rather than to concrete, identifiable causes. This paper examines the impact of such "uncertainty attribution" on stock market uncertainty. It helps assess whether the widely held belief in the informativeness of managerial explanations still holds as attribution targets shift from informative to uninformative. We develop a causality-sensitive BERT model to measure firm-year uncertainty attribution intensity based on MD&A texts of U.S. public firms (2004-2023). Event study results show that uncertainty attribution in disclosures raises stock market uncertainty. We rule out that this increase stems from higher volatility in firm fundamentals. Instead, an information choice in beauty contest model and additional empirical evidence indicate an informational mechanism: lower-precision public disclosures resulting from uncertainty attribution prompt investors to rely more on dispersed private signals. Our study is among the first to demonstrate how managerial attribution shapes disclosure informativeness and identifies a novel channel through which uncertainty is transmitted from the real economy to financial markets.

title: Board Governance in Complex Environments: Institutional Design, Oversight, and Resilience in an Era of Uncertainty

detail.title: Board Governance in Complex Environments: Institutional Design, Oversight, and Resilience in an Era of Uncertainty
detail.abstract:
Board governance has always required judgment under uncertainty. What has changed is the scale and simultaneity of the pressures boards now face: geopolitical fragmentation, technological disruption, stakeholder complexity, and an ESG landscape that continues to evolve faster than most governance frameworks can adapt. 
This guide identifies ten governance practices that distinguish boards capable of sustained institutional leadership from those that default to procedural compliance. The practices are drawn from governance research, practitioner experience, and institutional frameworks published by the OECD, National Association of Corporate Directors (NACD), International Corporate Governance Network (ICGN), and leading practitioner research from McKinsey & Company, Deloitte, Spencer Stuart, and other leading governance authorities. They are presented not as a checklist, but as a set of design principles-the organizational choices that determine whether a board functions as a governance system or as a ratification body.

title:
Toward a Physics of Liquidity Environments:
Environmental Architecture in Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT)
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Toward a Physics of Liquidity Environments:
Environmental Architecture in Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT)
detail.abstract:
Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT) was initially developed as a framework for studying liquidity redistribution processes within market systems. However, the progressive evolution of WLRT gradually revealed a broader environmental interpretation in which markets may be understood not merely as price-generation mechanisms, but as interacting liquidity environments possessing internal structure, fragility concentration, compensatory architecture, transmission constraints, and cross-environment propagation dynamics.

This paper introduces the foundational direction of a prospective research program referred to as Physics of Liquidity Environments (PLE).

The work proposes a transition from price-centric interpretation toward environment-centric redistribution analysis, where liquidity environments become the principal analytical objects and price is treated as a local observable projection of deeper redistribution processes occurring within interacting redistribution systems.

The paper introduces the foundational environmental ontology of:
liquidity environments,
liquidity carriers,
environmental conductivity,
redistribution pressure,
coupling structures,
transmission thresholds,
hybrid environments,
embedded environments,
and multi-scale redistribution dynamics.

Special attention is devoted to:
fragility propagation,
compensation architecture,
cross-environment interaction,
cascading redistribution dynamics,
phase transitions,
and propagation across interconnected environmental layers.

The paper intentionally does not present a finalized universal physical theory or deterministic predictive framework. Instead, it establishes:
a foundational environmental architecture,
a structural redistribution framework,
and a research roadmap for future development of environmental redistribution analysis.

Physics of Liquidity Environments (PLE) is therefore introduced not as a completed theory, but as an emerging structural research direction developing from the ontological and architectural foundations established within WLRT.

title: The Ramification Index: RAM Prices, Oligopoly Cycles, and the Downstream Consequences of Semiconductor Pricing as an Economic Signal

detail.title: The Ramification Index: RAM Prices, Oligopoly Cycles, and the Downstream Consequences of Semiconductor Pricing as an Economic Signal

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Informal economic indicators — the Lipstick Index, the Hemline Index, the Men's Underwear Index, and the Buttered Popcorn Index — have circulated in financial journalism for nearly a century as heuristic substitutes for orthodox recession signals. Each is built on consumer-demand folk psychology, each is trailing or noisy, and each has failed at least once in the past two decades. We propose a new indicator built instead on the supply side of the world's most financialised commodity: dynamic random-access memory (DRAM). We call it the Ramification Index — a name chosen deliberately. In algebraic number theory, the ramification index measures how a prime ideal branches and proliferates through a field extension: a single algebraic object whose local behaviour determines structure at a distance. We borrow the term because DRAM pricing works the same way: a price movement set by three firms in Seoul and Boise branches outward — into server capex, consumer electronics, AI infrastructure, and eventually the broader economy. The "RAM" in Ramification Index is not accidental. We define the index as the year-on-year log change in the three-firm oligopoly's average selling price per gigabyte, and reconstruct it annually for 1980-2026 using McCallum's canonical dataset, Federal Reserve price deflator work, and TrendForce contract and spot ASPs. We compare the Ramification Index against the four incumbent folk indices and the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) recession chronology. The index identifies all six NBER recessions since 1980, leads the cycle by a median of one to three quarters, and — unlike the folk indices — does not rely on consumer behaviour, fashion narration, or single-firm reporting. We argue that as memory has become the scarcest input into artificial-intelligence capital expenditure, DRAM pricing has the structural preconditions to serve as a genuine leading macro signal rather than a curiosity.

detail.abstract: Nassim Nicholas Taleb has argued that human cognition systematically underestimates extreme events by applying Gaussian models-suited to what he calls "Mediocristan"-to domains governed by power-law dynamics, which he terms "Extremistan." This paper argues that the same epistemological failure operates structurally within medicine, and specifically within evidencebased medicine (EBM). Drawing on Thomas Kuhn's theory of scientific paradigms and Karl Popper's principle of falsificationism, we examine how treatment-resistant conditions-chronic pain and fibromyalgia in particular-may represent the human cost of EBM's structural blind spots. We further present the anatomical discovery of the interstitium in 2018 as a documented medical instance of what Taleb calls "silent evidence": a structure present in every human body that remained systematically invisible for five centuries, not because it did not exist, but because the standard methods of observation eliminated it from view.

detail.abstract: Nigeria is one of Africa's most dynamic health economies, with a rapidly expanding digital health sector and growing deployment of artificial intelligence tools in clinical settings-from AI-assisted diagnostics in teaching hospitals to algorithmic triage in private facilities. Yet Nigeria's regulatory framework for clinical AI accountability contains significant and largely unexamined gaps. Existing legislation-including the National Health Act (2014), the Nigeria Data Protection Act (2023), the Medical and Dental Practitioners Act, and the National Health Insurance Authority Act-was designed for human clinical decision-making and does not establish clear lines of accountability when AI systems contribute to clinical harm. This paper conducts a structured policy gap analysis of Nigeria's clinical AI governance landscape, applying the Clinical AI Accountability Framework developed in Working Paper No. 1 of this series (Adebiyi, 2026a). The analysis identifies four critical governance gaps: the absence of a named decision ownership requirement; the lack of mandatory AI-specific validation standards for Nigerian patient populations; the absence of AI incident reporting obligations; and the underspecification of patient rights in AI-assisted clinical settings. The paper proposes five regulatory pathways through which Nigeria can close these gaps within its existing institutional architecture without requiring new primary legislation.

detail.abstract: This white paper analyzes aggregate coding results from a six-month review of Reddit discussions concerning oral and sublingual ketamine therapy. The analysis identifies recurring patient-reported themes, including dosing uncertainty, gastrointestinal side effects, bladder and urinary concerns, provider responsiveness, pharmacy variability, cost concerns, treatment tolerance, and integration support. Because the underlying source material concerns health-related Reddit discussions, the public dataset excludes usernames, post URLs, direct quotations, raw Reddit text, post-level records, and coder notes from individual posts. The findings should not be interpreted as prevalence estimates for all oral or sublingual ketamine patients. They are best understood as a signal-detection and patient-experience analysis from a self-selected online community.

detail.abstract: Falls represent a critical biomedical challenge for aging populations, often leading to severe injury or longlife scenarios if assistance is delayed. While fall prevention strategies focus on gait analysis, effective post-impact fall detection is essential for ensuring timely emergency escalation. Ambient vision-based systems offer a compelling alternative to wearable sensors by enabling reliable, passive monitoring without compliance burdens; however, widespread deployment faces significant hurdles regarding privacy, scalability, and system reliability. This paper proposes SOLA: Skeleton-based Optimized LSTM for Action recognition, a resource-efficient, privacy-centric pipeline designed for local execution in multicamera environments. Rather than relying on cloud processing or expensive dedicated workstations per room, SOLA optimizes the trade-off between computational demand and classification precision to enable robust operation on cost-effective local hardware. By synergizing skeletal pose estimation with an evolutionary-optimized LSTM network, the architecture minimizes false alarms, a crucial requirement for dependable emergency alerting. Furthermore, the lightweight design ensures that the system remains operational during network outages or partial infrastructure failures, prioritizing safety in worst-case scenarios. Experimental results on the GMDCSA-24 dataset demonstrate that SOLA achieves superior inference speed and low false-positive rates, offering a scalable solution for privacypreserving, decentralized home monitoring.

detail.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is widely used in medical diagnosis; however, speckle noise significantly reduces image clarity and diagnostic reliability. This study proposes a hybrid spatial-frequency domain filtering approach that combines spatial prediction filtering with frequency-domain enhancement to improve noise suppression while preserving structural details. The method integrates wavelet-based decomposition with spatial adaptive filtering to address limitations in conventional denoising techniques. Experimental evaluation on 300 clinical ultrasound images demonstrates a PSNR improvement of 18-25% over traditional methods, SSIM increase from 0.78 to 0.91, and edge preservation improvement of 22%. The findings indicate that the proposed hybrid approach provides a balanced and effective solution for enhancing clinical ultrasound imaging quality.

detail.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is widely used in medical diagnostics due to its non-invasive nature and real-time capability; however, its effectiveness is significantly limited by speckle noise, which degrades image quality and obscures critical anatomical details (Talukder et al., 2013). This study evaluates and optimizes multiple speckle noise reduction techniques, including spatial domain filters, frequency domain approaches, hybrid spatial-frequency methods, and emerging AI-based models. A comparative analysis was conducted to assess their performance in noise suppression, edge preservation, and tumor boundary clarity. The results demonstrate that hybrid filtering techniques and AI-assisted models consistently outperform traditional methods, achieving superior noise reduction while preserving structural and diagnostic features. Hybrid methods achieved 18-25% improvement in tumor detection accuracy over traditional filters, while AI-based models achieved 30-40% improvement. In particular, these advanced approaches enhance the visibility and delineation of tumor boundaries, which is critical for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Toward an In-Silico Neuroscience of Intelligence Analysis: TRIBE v2 Predictions of Stress and Persuasion in Intelligence-Grade Media

detail.title: Toward an In-Silico Neuroscience of Intelligence Analysis: TRIBE v2 Predictions of Stress and Persuasion in Intelligence-Grade Media
detail.abstract: We present the first application of Meta's TRIBE v2 brain encoding model to intelligence-grade and politically charged media stimuli. TRIBE v2 is a tri-modal foundation model trained on over 1,000 hours of fMRI recordings from 720 subjects, capable of predicting cortical brain activity in response to video, audio, and text without requiring physical brain scanning equipment. Using an in-silico neuroscience framework, we design two experiments to probe distinct neural response patterns across four real-world video stimuli representing different stress levels and communication strategies. In Experiment 1 (Intelligence Analyst Profile), we compare predicted brain responses to a highstress acoustic warfare stimulus (Lebanon attack footage, max: 0.48, mean: 0.020) against a lowstress diplomatic speech (John Kerry on Israel, max: 1.02, mean: 0.057). Results reveal that highstress content significantly suppresses prefrontal cortical activation, while analytically demanding diplomatic content engages broader cortical networks with substantially higher activation intensity. In Experiment 2 (General Public Profile), we compare an official government communication (Pentagon briefing, max: 0.97, mean: 0.051) against emotionally manipulative political messaging (Netanyahu addressing Iranians, max: 0.86, mean: 0.049). Results show that official language activates wider auditory and language networks, whereas manipulative content concentrates activation in narrower emotional processing regions. Our findings demonstrate that distinct media types produce measurably different neural signatures, and that TRIBE v2 represents a powerful, scalable tool for intelligence community applications including analyst performance research, media threat assessment, and the neuroscientific study of propaganda. To our knowledge, this is among the first studies to apply a predictive brain encoding model to intelligence and national security media contexts.

title: The Ramication Index: RAM Prices, Oligopoly Cycles, and the Downstream Consequences of Semiconductor Pricing as an Economic Signal (Version 2: The Bifurcated Index, Granger Causality, and the 2025-2026 Supply-Side Divergence)

detail.title: The Ramication Index: RAM Prices, Oligopoly Cycles, and the Downstream Consequences of Semiconductor Pricing as an Economic Signal (Version 2: The Bifurcated Index, Granger Causality, and the 2025-2026 Supply-Side Divergence)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
Three firms — Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron — control 95% of the world's dynamic random-access memory. Every quarter, their pricing decisions ripple outward through server costs, AI compute budgets, consumer electronics, and ultimately GDP. For a century, economists have tracked lipstick sales, hemline lengths, underwear purchases, and movie tickets as informal recession signals. Every one of these folk indices depends on consumer psychology. Every one of them broke during COVID-19.

The Ramification Index replaces them with something that doesn't break.

Defined as the year-on-year log change in DRAM average selling price, the index is named for three things simultaneously: the commodity (RAM), the economic consequences (ramifications), and the formal algebraic invariant from number theory — the ramification index that measures how a prime ideal branches through a field extension. A DRAM price shock works the same way: set by three firms in Seoul and Boise, it branches outward through every layer of the information economy before reaching the macroeconomy.

This second version introduces seven major extensions: (1) a bifurcated index splitting Commodity DRAM from AI/HBM pricing to capture the structural decoupling since 2024; (2) Granger causality tests showing the index leads GDP growth at 1–3 quarter lags (F = 5.83, p = 0.004); (3) a full case study of the 2025–2026 "RAMageddon" — the sharpest positive reading in 46 years, with contract prices surging 90–95% QoQ while the broader economy weakened; (4) the documented criminal history of DRAM price-fixing; (5) a formalized algebraic framework; (6) an assessment of photonic disruption risk; and (7) robustness checks including a NAND flash placebo test.

The Ramification Index identifies all six NBER recessions since 1980. No folk index signals more than three. The folk indices measure the leaves. This measures the root.

title: Environmental policies and firm productivity: Reconciling aggregate effects in the EU
affiliations: University of Graz

detail.title: Environmental policies and firm productivity: Reconciling aggregate effects in the EU
detail.abstract: Empirical evidence on the productivity effects of environmental regulation remains inconclusive, with mixed findings across studies. Using a large-scale panel of EU firms from 2013 to 2022, this paper examines how environmental policy stringency affects firm-level productivity. Productivity is estimated from production functions and regressed on policy stringency, measured using the OECD Climate Actions and Policies Measurement Framework, in a dynamic distributed-lag panel framework. Baseline estimates point to small and often statistically insignificant aggregate effects that are highly sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, reflecting policy–macro co-movement. Decomposing sectoral policies by instrument type suggests potentially offsetting effects, which attenuate once policy–macro co-movement is accounted for. Allowing for sectoral heterogeneity, however, reveals pronounced differences across industries, with more negative responses in input-intensive and regulation-exposed sectors and more positive ones in less exposed, more flexible sectors. These findings indicate that aggregate estimates mask economically meaningful heterogeneity across sectors and policy instruments, thereby helping to reconcile the mixed empirical evidence.

publicationDetails.journalName: Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study investigates whether the expanded effective availability of generative AI influences offline sexual crime. We exploit the May 2023 launch of the ChatGPT iOS application in Japan as a quasi-exogenous shock to GenAI accessibility and combine monthly crime statistics from Japan’s National Police Agency with platform-level engagement data from one of the country’s largest digital creator platforms. Using difference-in-differences and difference-in-difference-in-differences models, we estimate the effect of GenAI diffusion on reported rape incidence relative to murder and examine whether this effect varies with aggregate engagement in AI-generated explicit content. The results indicate a statistically significant post-launch increase in reported rape relative to murder, amounting to approximately 12 additional cases per month. Moreover, this effect is significantly amplified during periods of greater engagement with AI-generated adult sexual content. Supplemental analyses further show that engagement with minor-tagged AI-generated explicit content is associated with even stronger post-launch increases, particularly for offenses involving victims under age 20. Collectively, the findings are more consistent with stimulation and social learning mechanisms than with cathartic substitution. The study contributes early causal evidence that generative AI may produce harmful offline behavioral externalities and underscores the need for regulatory and platform-level safeguards.

title: The AI Is Not Your Legal Assistant: A Proposed Model Rule Comment for AI-Assisted Legal Practice

detail.title: The AI Is Not Your Legal Assistant: A Proposed Model Rule Comment for AI-Assisted Legal Practice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author founded and operates PriorityLex, LLC, which trains legal professionals in AI-assisted practice and places AI-enabled legal assistants with US law firms. The architecture proposed in this paper is the framework PriorityLex uses internally. This relationship is disclosed in the author footnote of the paper.

detail.abstract: Every jurisdiction addressing artificial intelligence in legal practice has framed AI through the legal assistant analogy of Model Rule 5.3 and prescribed behavioral verification without specifying what competent AI use requires at the operational level. The research record from human-factors engineering and cognitive psychology shows that the supervisory frame is structurally mismatched to AI oversight and that just telling lawyers to verify the AI predictably fails to improve outcomes. This paper proposes a Model Rule Comment to Rule 1.1 and an accompanying nine-section guidance document that replaces the supervision analogy with an architecture-competence framework. The comment organizes AI-assisted practice across four layers: (0) configuration, (1) deterministic verification, (2) independent analytical review, and (3) concentrated review by the lawyer. The architecture’s central move is the generation-verification distinction that AI systems are unreliable generators of legal analysis but effective verifiers of it, capable of deterministic citation checking against authoritative databases and structured analytical review under separation from the original reasoning chain. The architecture deploys AI for the verification tasks it performs well, concentrating the lawyer’s professional judgment on the items the verification layers flag rather than dispersing it across undifferentiated review of the full output. The comment establishes a procedural safe harbor modeled on the technology-assisted review doctrine developed in Da Silva Moore, Rio Tinto, Hyles, and In re Biomet: procedural competence satisfies the lawyer’s obligation when the process is properly designed and executed, even where the system produces an error the architecture did not prevent. The guidance document operationalizes the comment with verification standards for each layer, a documentation regime that spans all four layers, an education floor, and operational-competence provisions permitting delegation to supervised legal assistants. This architecture was originally developed in Potter, The Verification Duty as Architectural Specification (2026).

title: Exchange Rate Regime Choice in Small Oil-Based Open Economies under Geopolitical Fragmentation -Evidence from Oman
affiliations: and King's University College at Western University

detail.title: Exchange Rate Regime Choice in Small Oil-Based Open Economies under Geopolitical Fragmentation -Evidence from Oman
detail.abstract: We revisit the performance of Oman's U.S. dollar peg in an environment characterised by oil-price volatility, U.S. monetary tightening, and rising geopolitical risk. Using monthly data from 2014 to 2023 and identified external shocks following Baumeister and Hamilton (2019), Bauer and Swanson (2023), and Caldara and Iacoviello (2022), we estimate the transmission of these shocks to Omani inflation and import dynamics in a local-projections framework. Two robust findings emerge. First, U.S. monetary policy transmits cleanly and economically large to Omani consumer prices: a one-standard-deviation Federal Reserve tightening surprise reduces year-on-year CPI inflation by approximately 2.5 percentage points at the 16-month horizon, an order of magnitude larger than any single oil-market or geopolitical-risk effect. The peg's core nominal-anchor function is intact. Second, the transmission of geopolitical-risk shocks to Omani inflation has structurally increased in the post-2018 sub-period, with the interaction coefficient peaking at +0.95 percentage points at the two-year horizon and surviving HAC, block-residual bootstrap, and Covid-exclusion inference. We additionally document, in contrast to the conventional GCC currency-policy narrative, that Oman's import structure has concentrated within the USD-pegged bloc over 2005-2025 (from 38% to 53%) rather than reorienting toward Asia. The policy implication is what we call "maintain the peg, address the gap": the peg's monetary function does not justify regime change, while the eroded geopolitical-risk insulation calls for complementary instruments-reserve diversification, trade-invoicing flexibility, and supply-chain resilience-that operate alongside the peg rather than through it.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how policy-induced supply-chain shocks affect firms' performances, using the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) as a source of exogenous variation. Using UK microdata on firm-level goods and services trade linked to firm's outcomes and employer-employee records, we document a sharp decline in firms’ imports of intermediate goods from the EU after 2021. We then show that firms more exposed to EU input sourcing experience declines in employment and sales, with corresponding effects on workers’ hours and pay. These impacts are heterogeneous across occupations, with larger losses concentrated among lower-skilled roles. Interestingly, we find that firms' services activities play an important role in mediating the impact of GVCs disruptions. On the one hand, these firms experience smaller declines in intermediate inputs imports; on the other hand, they experience stronger negative reactions to the overall GVC shock.

detail.title: Demand for Conversational AI

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We estimate demand for five conversational AI use cases — administrative assistance, studying, wellness, friendship, and romance — using a preregistered, within-respondent conjoint experiment in a U.S. online sample (N=1,989). Purpose dominates interest: instrumental uses rank highest, romance lowest. Free pricing raises interest sharply but is attenuated for relational purposes, revealing non-monetary signaling costs that price reductions cannot eliminate. Privacy and personalization shift demand; interaction modality does not. Second-order beliefs exceed own interest in proportion to the purpose penalty, consistent with a single stigma parameter suppressing stated below latent demand. Corrected consumer surplus for a free romantic companion turns positive once suppression costs are recovered — the welfare mirror image of social media’s collective trap.

title: The Heterogeneous Bank Lending Channel of Monetary Policy
affiliations: , University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), ,  and Banco de España

detail.title: The Heterogeneous Bank Lending Channel of Monetary Policy

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: How does heterogeneity in banks' interest-rate risk exposure shape monetary policy transmission? We develop a quantitative macroeconomic model of heterogeneous banks to answer this question. We establish an irrelevance result: differences in interest-rate risk exposure between fixed- and variable-rate banking systems matter for transmission only when bank solvency concerns become relevant. Calibrating the model to the euro area, we show that idiosyncratic default risk pushes a substantial share of banks toward the solvency threshold, making heterogeneity quantitatively important. When policy rates rise, fixed-rate banks suffer net interest margin compression — funding costs increase while legacy loan income stays unchanged — eroding capital and triggering sharper deleveraging. The lending elasticity to monetary policy is one-third larger in fixed-rate economies. The effects extend to financial stability: tightening raises bank failure rates in fixed-rate systems while lowering them in variable-rate systems. The results provide a rationale for macroprudential and monetary policy coordination and for monetary policy gradualism.
